description: HPR Fig. 18. Two guarded definitions of x both reach `int y = x`; A swaps the two if-blocks (and edits u), B edits w. G_M carries def-order edges in BOTH directions - `x = 1 ->do(int y = x) x = 2` from B and the reverse from A - so Type I catches the reorder, which is where HPR put reorder detection (their third seed rule, SS4.1.2). Without those edges Type I is blind to it, because statement ORDER is nowhere else in G_M's edges. Type II still fires independently (def-order), so both are pinned.
category: silent bad textual merge - semantics catches it (def-order, via Type I)
